answers.label: Q1
answers.finalAnswer: Two numbers whose HCF is 1; e.g. (4, 9) and (8, 15)
answers.solution:
Co-prime numbers are two numbers whose only common factor is 1, that is, their HCF is 1. The numbers themselves need not be prime.

Pair 1: 4 and 9. Factors of 4 are 1, 2, 4; factors of 9 are 1, 3, 9. The only common factor is 1, so HCF \((4, 9) = 1\).

Pair 2: 8 and 15. Factors of 8 are 1, 2, 4, 8; factors of 15 are 1, 3, 5, 15. The only common factor is 1, so HCF \((8, 15) = 1\).

So, co-prime numbers are numbers with HCF 1, for example (4, 9) and (8, 15).

\(\left(x - \frac{1}{x}\right)^2 = x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2} - 2 = 51 - 2 = 49\)

So \(x - \frac{1}{x} = 7\) (taking the positive root; the negative root gives \(-7\)).

Use \(a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)^3 + 3ab(a - b)\) with \(a = x\), \(b = \frac{1}{x}\), \(ab = 1\):

\(x^3 - \frac{1}{x^3} = \left(x - \frac{1}{x}\right)^3 + 3\left(x - \frac{1}{x}\right)\)

\(= 7^3 + 3 \times 7 = 343 + 21 = 364\)

(If \(x - \frac{1}{x} = -7\), the value is \(-364\).)

So, the answer is 364.

Cross-multiply: \((2 + x)(7 - x) = (5 - x)(4 + x)\)

Left side: \(14 - 2x + 7x - x^2 = 14 + 5x - x^2\)

Right side: \(20 + 5x - 4x - x^2 = 20 + x - x^2\)

So \(14 + 5x - x^2 = 20 + x - x^2\)

The \(x^2\) terms cancel: \(5x - x = 20 - 14\), so \(4x = 6\)

\(x = \frac{6}{4} = \frac{3}{2}\)

Check: the denominator \((5 - \frac{3}{2})(4 + \frac{3}{2})\) is not zero.

So, \(x = \frac{3}{2}\).

answers.label: Q9
answers.finalAnswer: Stream 3 km/hr; boat in still water 8 km/hr
answers.solution:
Let the upstream speed be \(u\) km/hr and the downstream speed be \(d\) km/hr.

\(\frac{30}{u} + \frac{44}{d} = 10\) ... (1)

\(\frac{40}{u} + \frac{55}{d} = 13\) ... (2)

Put \(p = \frac{1}{u}\), \(q = \frac{1}{d}\): \(30p + 44q = 10\) and \(40p + 55q = 13\).

Multiply (1) by 4: \(120p + 176q = 40\)

Multiply (2) by 3: \(120p + 165q = 39\)

Subtract: \(11q = 1\), so \(q = \frac{1}{11}\) and \(d = 11\) km/hr.

Then \(30p = 10 - 44 \times \frac{1}{11} = 10 - 4 = 6\), so \(p = \frac{1}{5}\) and \(u = 5\) km/hr.

Boat speed \(b\), stream speed \(s\): \(b + s = 11\) and \(b - s = 5\).

Adding: \(2b = 16\), \(b = 8\); so \(s = 3\).

So, the speed of the stream is 3 km/hr and the speed of the boat in still water is 8 km/hr.

LCM of 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12:

\(8 = 2^3\), \(12 = 2^2 \times 3\), \(10 = 2 \times 5\), so LCM = \(2^3 \times 3 \times 5 = 120\).

A number leaving remainder 2 with each is of the form \(120k + 2\).

It must be divisible by 13. Since \(120 = 13 \times 9 + 3\), \(120k + 2\) leaves remainder \(3k + 2\) on division by 13 (reduced mod 13).

Try \(k = 1, 2, 3, \ldots\): \(3k + 2 = 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23, 26\). The first multiple of 13 is 26, at \(k = 8\).

Number = \(120 \times 8 + 2 = 962\).

Check: \(962 = 13 \times 74\), and \(962 - 2 = 960 = 120 \times 8\).

So, the least such number is 962.

answers.label: Q29
answers.finalAnswer: 8 minutes (reading the full time as 18 min; as printed, 9 min is impossible)
answers.solution:
As printed, the question cannot be done: even with both pipes open the whole time, in 9 minutes they fill only \(9\left(\frac{1}{24} + \frac{1}{32}\right) = 9 \times \frac{7}{96} = \frac{21}{32}\) of the tank. Both pipes together need \(\frac{96}{7} \approx 13.7\) minutes, so the tank can never be full in 9 minutes. The time is most likely meant to be 18 minutes; that version is solved below.

Pipe A fills \(\frac{1}{24}\) of the tank per minute; pipe B fills \(\frac{1}{32}\).

A runs for all 18 minutes: it fills \(\frac{18}{24} = \frac{3}{4}\) of the tank.

B must fill the rest: \(1 - \frac{3}{4} = \frac{1}{4}\).

Let B run for \(t\) minutes: \(\frac{t}{32} = \frac{1}{4}\), so \(t = 8\).

(With 9 minutes as printed, the same method gives \(t = 32 \times \frac{5}{8} = 20\) minutes, which is more than 9, confirming the misprint.)

So, pipe B should be closed after 8 minutes.

answers.label: Q.30
answers.solution:
The third denominator is printed as \(x^{c}\, x^{-a} + 1\) with a plus sign missing; following the pattern of the first two terms it is \(x^{c} + x^{-a} + 1\).

Given \(a + b + c = 0\), so \(a + b = -c\) and \(-a - c = b\).

First term: multiply top and bottom by \(x^{b}\):

\(\frac{1}{x^{a} + x^{-b} + 1} = \frac{x^{b}}{x^{a+b} + 1 + x^{b}} = \frac{x^{b}}{x^{-c} + 1 + x^{b}}\)

Second term is already \(\frac{1}{x^{b} + x^{-c} + 1}\).

Third term: multiply top and bottom by \(x^{-c}\):

\(\frac{1}{x^{c} + x^{-a} + 1} = \frac{x^{-c}}{1 + x^{-a-c} + x^{-c}} = \frac{x^{-c}}{1 + x^{b} + x^{-c}}\)

Now all three have the same denominator \(x^{b} + x^{-c} + 1\):

Sum = \(\frac{x^{b} + 1 + x^{-c}}{x^{b} + x^{-c} + 1} = 1\)

So, the value is 1.
